C118 (off-season) · A's · rumor · Leo Valdez (C): The A's are being linked to one of the top names on the free agent market, catcher Leo Valdez. Valdez has spent his career in Philadelphia, the team Oakland beat in five games for the seventh World Series title. He is 26, born in Venezuela, a first round pick in 2034, rated 99 overall with A potential. He bats and throws right and hits to the whole field. In 2041 he hit .285 with 158 hits, 25 doubles, 31 homeruns, 88 RBI, 78 walks and 13 steals in 555 at bats, with a .379 on-base and .497 slugging. Over his last five seasons he has never hit below .285 or finished with fewer than 31 homeruns: .292 with 37 homeruns in 2037, .314 in 2038, .301 with 38 homeruns and 111 RBI in 2039, and .289 with 36 homeruns and 112 RBI in 2040. His career line reads .294 with 1,089 hits, 222 homeruns and 636 RBI. Against left-handed pitching his contact rating is a perfect 99. Behind the plate he has a 91 arm and 85 blocking, and his 97 durability shows in the box score: 140 or more games every season since 2037. | Stats: Leo Valdez/2041/147G/555AB/.285AVG/158H/25 2B/31HR/88RBI/78BB/111SO/13SB/.379OBP/.497SLG, Leo Valdez/career/975G/3708AB/.294AVG/1089H/182 2B/222HR/636RBI/92SB/.375OBP/.530SLG, Leo Valdez/99OVR/A potential/age 26/99 CON L/91ARM/85BLK/97DUR | Team record: - | Streak: -

C117 (off-season) · A's · re-signing · Mariano Rosales (CP): Mariano Rosales came to Oakland in C39 as the young arm in the trade that sent five-time All-Star closer Edmundo Pena to Baltimore, a 26-year-old with A potential and an 89 overall, and the question then was whether he was ready to replace a legend. In C83 he was named the closer on a one-year, $10.1 million deal with free agency waiting at the end of it. That free agency is off the table now. Rosales has signed a five-year contract at $17.6 million a year, $88 million in all, running 2042 through 2046 with no contract option, and he would not reach free agency until 2047. He earned the raise in the season the A's went 127-35 and won the seventh World Series. Rosales went 8-3 with 42 saves and a 1.84 ERA in 63.2 innings, struck out 82 and walked 14, finished with 1.7 WAR and made the All-Star team, one of seven A's selected in C99. The one mark on the year came in World Series game 2, when he and Clark Saryan each gave up 2 runs in relief of Travis Coles. He goes into the new deal at 27, with a 95 overall that is still climbing, a 96 mph four-seam fastball, a 94 mph two-seamer and an 84 mph changeup. The Utah-born right-hander, a second round pick in 2035, lives in Jack London. The deal also answers part of the bullpen question this page raised in C114, whether the A's would spend on a high-end arm or turn the late innings over to rookies Saryan and Julio Valencia. The ninth inning stays with Rosales. | Stats: Mariano Rosales/5yr/$88M/$17.6M AAV/2042-2046/FA 2047, Mariano Rosales/2041/63.2IP/1.84ERA/8-3/42SV/82SO/14BB/1.7WAR/All-Star, Mariano Rosales/95OVR/age 27/$10.1M 2041, Mariano Rosales/4-seam 96mph/2-seam 94mph/changeup 84mph | Team record: - | Streak: -

C117 (early-season) · Oaks · team-update · Wilson Shepard (Coach): The Oaks are winning games after halftime, and they have done it since the first game in franchise history. Against Charlotte at home in game one, in front of a sold-out crowd, they trailed 36-32 at the half and 60-49 after three, then scored 36 in the fourth and held the Hornets to 22 to win 85-82. In Detroit they trailed 43-37 at the half and won the second half 54-35 for a 91-78 win. At Golden State they trailed 59-44 at the half, the biggest halftime deficit they have come back from, then won the third 30-19 and the fourth 24-18, outscoring the Warriors 54-37 after the break to win 98-96. In Philadelphia they trailed 82-80 going into the fourth, scored 40 and held the 76ers to 24 for a 120-106 win. In Denver in C116 they were already up 23 after three and still put up 42 in the fourth of a franchise-record 147-114 win. Even the Indiana loss showed it. Down 61-42 at the half and 82-62 after three, the Oaks scored 38 in the fourth, won the quarter 38-22 and came within four, 104-100. Through 13 games the Oaks have won the fourth quarter 10 times, lost it twice and tied it once. One of the two losses was the Orlando game, which was already decided at 101-76 after three. The other was the home loss to San Antonio, tied 90-90 going into the fourth before the Spurs won the quarter by 9. Wilson Shepard's young team finishes. In Indiana a 19-point halftime hole was too much. In Golden State a 15-point hole was not. | Stats: Oaks/game 1 vs CHA/down 60-49 after three/won 4th 36-22/won 85-82, Oaks/at DET/down 43-37 at half/won 2nd half 54-35/won 91-78, Oaks/at GSW/down 59-44 at half/won 2nd half 54-37, Oaks/at PHI/down 82-80 after three/won 4th 40-24, Oaks/at IND/down 82-62 after three/won 4th 38-22/lost 104-100, Oaks/at DEN C116/won 4th 42-32, Oaks/vs SA/tied 90-90 after three/lost 4th by 9, Oaks/4th quarters 10-2-1 in 13 games | Team record: 11-2 | Streak: W2

C117 (early-season) · Oaks · player-feature · Austin Reaves (SG): Austin Reaves is the highest-paid player on the Oaks at $30 million a year, and this cycle he played like it. He led the Oaks in scoring in both games of C117. Against Denver at home he scored 32 in just 22 minutes on 8 of 14, 6 of 10 from three and 10 of 10 at the line, without a turnover. Then at Golden State he had 23 points, 6 rebounds, 5 assists and 3 steals in 33 minutes as the Oaks came back from 15 down at the half to win 98-96. Through 13 games he has led the Oaks in scoring or shared the lead six times: 23 in New York, tied with AJ Dybantsa; 23 in Washington and 19 in Indiana, tied with Adash Stanley; 20 in Toronto; 32 against Denver; and 23 at Golden State. He does it without needing the ball to himself. In the first game in franchise history, the 85-82 home win over Charlotte, he had 20 points and 9 rebounds on 6 of 12, 4 of 9 from three and 4 of 4 at the line without a turnover. He handed out 10 assists in Detroit, had 9 rebounds and 3 steals with his 23 in New York, and in the 147-114 franchise-record win in Denver he scored 27 on 11 of 14, a perfect 5 of 5 from three, with 12 assists. He also answers his bad nights. After going 4 of 14 in Philadelphia he scored 27 in Denver, and after 13 points and 4 turnovers in the home loss to San Antonio he scored 32 against Denver. Off the court Reaves lives in West Oakland, where he moved after buying first in Downtown. C117 (off-season) · A's · player-feature · Danny Horn (CF): In C73 Danny Horn said he was the best player in baseball. He was coming off a 2040 season of .280 with 32 homeruns, 98 RBI, 35 steals, a .524 slugging, an .879 OPS and 8.0 WAR, and the claim started an argument. In 2041 he made it for himself. The A's center fielder hit .338 with 210 hits, 48 doubles, 9 triples, 56 homeruns, 113 RBI, 152 runs and 80 stolen bases in 148 games, with a .382 on-base, .715 slugging and a 1.097 OPS. He was caught stealing only 9 times, struck out just 65 times in 671 plate appearances, and made one error in 1,279 innings in center field for a .997 fielding percentage. His 13.3 WAR is 5.3 more than the season he made the claim. He led the league in hits, doubles, homeruns, runs, stolen bases, slugging and OPS, and won the MVP, the Hank Aaron Award, the batting title, the home run title, his second Silver Slugger and his fourth All-Star selection. The start of his career looks nothing like it. Horn was a fourth round pick in 2029 who hit .166 in 58 games with Minnesota in 2033 and .192 there in 2034, then .214 and .198 in his first two seasons in Oakland. Since then he has hit .246, .259, .322, .280 and .338, and 28.8 of his 42.4 career WAR came in the last three seasons. His career line now reads .268 with 1,143 hits, 246 homeruns, 643 RBI and 208 steals in 1,122 games. He is 30, rated 99 overall, and signed at $37.8M a year through 2044 before free agency in 2045. Horn is also bringing back his wiffle ball tournament. It started in C79 in West Oakland, sponsored by Horn to celebrate the Stabilization Fund, and moved to Temescal, where Horn lives, in C80. The second annual tournament is in Dimond this year. | Stats: Danny Horn/2041/148G/621AB/.338AVG/210H/48 2B/9 3B/56HR/113RBI/152R/80SB/9CS/65SO/.382OBP/.715SLG/1.097OPS/13.3WAR, Danny Horn/2041 CF/1279 INN/1E/.997FLD%, Danny Horn/2040/.280AVG/32HR/98RBI/35SB/.524SLG/.879OPS/8.0WAR, Danny Horn/career/1122G/.268AVG/1143H/246HR/643RBI/208SB/42.4WAR, Danny Horn/99OVR/$37.8M through 2044/FA 2045 | Team record: - | Streak: -

C117 (off-season) · A's · re-signing · Vladimir Gonzalez (RF): The same cycle Mark Aitken left for Colorado, the A's locked up a player they intend to keep. Vladimir Gonzalez, the A's right fielder, has agreed to a five-year, $119 million contract, $23.8 million a year, avoiding arbitration. It is the biggest raise on the roster this off-season. Gonzalez made $2.7M in 2041, so the new deal adds $21.1M a year, almost exactly the $21.4M that came off the books when Aitken signed with the Rockies. Mike Paulson let a 33-year-old walk on a one-year deal and put the same money into a 28-year-old for five. He earned it. Gonzalez, born in the Dominican Republic, is a 92 overall right fielder coming off the best line of his career: .306 with 161 hits, 28 homeruns, 76 RBI, 17 steals and 4.7 WAR in 527 at bats, with only 60 strikeouts. That 4.7 WAR is more than Aitken's 3.2 and more than any A's hitter this page has written up this off-season. The deal also settles a question Gonzalez raised himself. In C113, with the outfield crowded behind him, he said he was not sure how his clutch performance would affect his chances, that "it's up to Paulson to decide," and named Desmond Morton and Frank Reyna as the players pushing him. He told the young guys, "you can't control what Paulson decides. You just control how you show up," and added, "I earned my spot, sure, but I remember what it was like trying to crack a crowded room." Five years answers who plays right field. It also means Reyna, Morton, JR Rosado and Kevin Clark, whose secondary positions include right field, are competing for left field and the bench. | Stats: Vladimir Gonzalez/5yr/$119M/$23.8M AAV/avoided arbitration, Vladimir Gonzalez/2041/527AB/.306AVG/161H/28HR/76RBI/17SB/60SO/4.7WAR, Vladimir Gonzalez/92OVR/age 28/$2.7M 2041 | Team record: - | Streak: -

C117 (off-season) · A's · roster-move · Mark Aitken (1B): The free agency question this page has carried since C112 has its answer, and it is not Oakland and it is not Anaheim. Mark Aitken has signed with the Colorado Rockies, one year for $21 million. The Angels were the team with the reported interest in C116, the A's were the team with the history, and Colorado is the team that closed. The money is almost exactly what he made in 2041, $21.4M, so this was never about Aitken being priced as a player in decline. He is coming off a .283 season with 153 hits, 33 homeruns, 87 RBI and 3.2 WAR in 540 at bats, a 93 overall first baseman with 3 Gold Gloves and the 2037 Playoff MVP, and he homered in the World Series that clinched the seventh title. The length is the detail that will be argued over. One year is a short commitment for a player at the top of the market, and it puts Aitken back in free agency after 2042. Whether that reads as a door left open or simply the deal that was there, he has not said. What it leaves behind in Oakland is bigger than a lineup spot. Aitken is an Oakland native who grew up swinging a bat in East Oakland. He owns his place in Jack London, where he lives with his wife and three kids. He has been the A's player rep and community liaison, and he runs Aitken Little Leaguers, free baseball for East Oakland kids heading into its sixth year. He showed up at city council and planning hearings, brought Benji Dillon to the DEIR session, was a major voice in the Baylight negotiations, and was the veteran who reached out to Kevin Clark the day Clark was called up. In C114 he wrote that "the number on the calendar means more than the number on my back," and that "the city has a way of holding on to its own, and I've been its own for a long, long time." This time the city did not hold on. For the A's, the move this page laid out in C116 now happens: Ernesto Quintero slides across the diamond to first base. That opens third base outright to the bat-or-glove contest between Kevin Clark, .327 in 55 at bats with 83 discipline and 87 clutch, and Giancarlo Hernandez, the 96 fielding glove from the Carmen Mesa trade. It also comes in the same off-season Vinnie Keane retired, which means the A's go into 2042 without the two longest-standing local voices in their clubhouse. Mike Paulson's choice is now on the record: Aitken walks, and the club trusts its young infield. | Stats: Mark Aitken/1yr/$21.0M 2042/Rockies, Mark Aitken/2041/540AB/.283AVG/153H/33HR/87RBI/3.2WAR, Mark Aitken/93OVR/$21.4M 2041/3 Gold Gloves/2037 Playoff MVP | Team record: - | Streak: -

C116 (early-season) · Oaks · team-update · Wilson Shepard (Coach), Adash Stanley (PG), T. Jerome (PG), Elliot Abraham (GM): Ten games into their first season, the Oakland Oaks are the number one team in the NBA.com power rankings, ranked first of all 31 teams, and holding the top spot from the week before. The rankings are built on season record and recent form, and the Oaks had both: 9-1 when they came out, 3-0 over the last week, 6-1 over the last two weeks. They earned it against real opponents. Four of the teams in the top nine are teams the Oaks have already beaten: Detroit, ranked 3rd, beaten 91-78 on the road; Oklahoma City, ranked 4th, beaten 101-95 in the Cup opener at home; New York, ranked 6th, beaten 115-93 on the road; and Philadelphia, ranked 8th, beaten 120-106 on the road after trailing by two going into the fourth. Ranked 2nd was San Antonio. The rankings only update once a week, and these came out a game behind. Since then the Spurs came into Oakland for a Cup game and won 126-117, handing the Oaks their first ever home loss. So number one is now 9-2, number two is 8-2, and the gap at the top is half a game. For an expansion team that went 0-9 through rookie camp and the preseason, with a first-year head coach and a first-time GM, being ranked first in the league at all is the story. | Stats: Oaks/NBA.com Power Ranking/#1 of 31/no change, Oaks/9-1 at ranking/3-0 last week/6-1 last two weeks/9-1 last month, Oaks/now 9-2 after Spurs loss, Oaks wins over ranked teams/DET #3/OKC #4/NYK #6/PHI #8 | Team record: 9-2 | Streak: L1

Jerome (PG), AJ Dybantsa (SF), Adash Stanley (PG), Wendell Carter Jr (C), Austin Reaves (SG), Dillon Brooks (SF), Harry Hayward (PF), Wilson Shepard (Coach): The Spurs handed the Oaks their first ever home loss. The Oaks trailed by 8 after a slow 20-point first, won the second 35-25 to lead 55-53 at the half, and it was tied 90-90 going into the fourth. Nine games into the real deal, the Oaks are 8-1, have won four straight and are 1-0 in the NBA Cup. They beat Charlotte 85-82 in the franchise's first game, coming back from 11 down after three, won in Detroit, New York and Washington, lost by four in Indiana after coming back from 20 down, then routed Toronto 135-75 and beat Oklahoma City, Orlando and Philadelphia. Shepard came in as the offensive specialist, but the early identity is defense: Charlotte scored 82, Detroit 78, Toronto 75 and Washington 62. He has also found rotation pieces nobody expected, like second-round rookie Harry Hayward, and kept the bench fresh, with nobody playing more than 28 minutes in the Toronto rout. After the opener he laughed that his ears were still ringing, then said the next loss could be a game away and the job was to build on the good and eliminate the bad. The other half of this story is the man above him. Mike Paulson is president of operations for an 8-1 expansion team, with Elliot Abraham running the day-to-day as GM, and he is also the GM of the A's in the middle of an offseason that has already seen Vinnie Keane retire, Carmen Mesa traded to the Phillies, Mark Aitken drawing Angels interest in free agency and Benji Dillon undecided. He also said the Draymond Green trade "wasn't ideal form" for a player the community reveres, and that Jerami Grant's status was a matter the league was looking into. C117 (off-season) · A's · player-feature · Danny Horn (CF): In C73 Danny Horn said he was the best player in baseball. He was coming off a 2040 season of .280 with 32 homeruns, 98 RBI, 35 steals, a .524 slugging, an .879 OPS and 8.0 WAR, and the claim started an argument. In 2041 he made it for himself. The A's center fielder hit .338 with 210 hits, 48 doubles, 9 triples, 56 homeruns, 113 RBI, 152 runs and 80 stolen bases in 148 games, with a .382 on-base, .715 slugging and a 1.097 OPS. He was caught stealing only 9 times, struck out just 65 times in 671 plate appearances, and made one error in 1,279 innings in center field for a .997 fielding percentage. His 13.3 WAR is 5.3 more than the season he made the claim. He led the league in hits, doubles, homeruns, runs, stolen bases, slugging and OPS, and won the MVP, the Hank Aaron Award, the batting title, the home run title, his second Silver Slugger and his fourth All-Star selection. The start of his career looks nothing like it. Horn was a fourth round pick in 2029 who hit .166 in 58 games with Minnesota in 2033 and .192 there in 2034, then .214 and .198 in his first two seasons in Oakland. Since then he has hit .246, .259, .322, .280 and .338, and 28.8 of his 42.4 career WAR came in the last three seasons. C116 (early-season) · Oaks · season-state · Wilson Shepard (Coach), Mike Paulson (President of Operations), Elliot Abraham (GM): Ten cycles ago this page was asking Wilson Shepard for answers. The Oaks went 0-4 in rookie camp and 0-5 in the preseason, 0-9 before they had played a game that counted, and in C109 the media wanted to know why the team was losing and why the full roster had never been on the floor together. Shepard, a first-year head coach who spent the previous season as an offensive assistant in Minnesota, kept saying the same thing. In C107 he said the Oaks would "catch people off guard this year." In C109 he said, "We're still finding our rhythm. The guys are putting in the work, and I'm confident we'll tighten up and be ready for the real deal. We're not getting the results we want, but we're not letting it get us down either." In C110, after the loss to Miami, he said the full team had yet to suit up as one, that opening night would show a team nobody had seen, and that he was not worried. The fans were. Nine games into the real deal, the Oaks are 8-1, have won four straight and are 1-0 in the NBA Cup. They beat Charlotte 85-82 in the franchise's first game, coming back from 11 down after three, won in Detroit, New York and Washington, lost by four in Indiana after coming back from 20 down, then routed Toronto 135-75 and beat Oklahoma City, Orlando and Philadelphia. They are scoring 109.9 a game and allowing 89.6, a margin of more than 20 points a night. The surprise is how they are winning. Shepard came in as the offensive specialist, but the early identity is defense: Charlotte scored 82, Detroit 78, Toronto 75 and Washington 62. He has also found rotation pieces nobody expected, like second-round rookie Harry Hayward, and kept the bench fresh, with nobody playing more than 28 minutes in the Toronto rout. After the opener he laughed that his ears were still ringing, then said the next loss could be a game away and the job was to build on the good and eliminate the bad. The other half of this story is the man above him. Mike Paulson is president of operations for an 8-1 expansion team, with Elliot Abraham running the day-to-day as GM, and he is also the GM of the A's in the middle of an offseason that has already seen Vinnie Keane retire, Carmen Mesa traded to the Phillies, Mark Aitken drawing Angels interest in free agency and Benji Dillon undecided. In C110 fans worried that a first-year coach, a first-time GM and a front office chief busy with a World Series run was too much uncertainty. So far the Oaks have answered that. Then there is Elliot Abraham, the first-time GM who has said almost nothing since C111. That cycle, with the team 0-9, he told the media nobody was panicking, that the losing was intentional and that every variation they tried was data for the long term. He also said the Draymond Green trade "wasn't ideal form" for a player the community reveres, and that Jerami Grant's status was a matter the league was looking into. In C112 Elias Varek confirmed Grant had failed his medical and credited Paulson and Abraham with building a quality team in one offseason. Abraham has not spoken since. His path here is not a typical basketball one: born in Port-au-Prince, Haiti, adopted young by an American family, MIT, the man who built the first successful professional pickleball league, then senior operations under Varek at Civis Systems and Paulson's day-to-day operator in his one season with the Chicago Bulls before Oakland hired him in C101. The Bulls beat his Oaks in the preseason in C110. He lives in Jack London, has been seen staying late in the clubhouse after wins, and around the waterfront he is still more of a familiar face than a public one. | Stats: Oaks/8-1/W4/109.9 PPG/89.6 OPP PPG/+20.3 margin, Oaks/0-4 rookie camp/0-5 preseason, Oaks/1-0 NBA Cup, Opponents held under 85/CHA 82/DET 78/TOR 75/WAS 62 | Team record: 8-1 | Streak: W4

Word around the league is that the Anaheim Angels have strong interest in Mark Aitken, the A's first baseman and one of the top free agents on the market at 93 overall. Aitken, 33, is coming off a contract year that looked nothing like a decline: .283 with 153 hits, 33 homeruns, 87 RBI and 3.2 WAR in 540 at bats, plus the 3 homerun night against the Phillies and homeruns in the World Series that clinched the seventh title. He made $21.4M in 2041, and any offer that pulls him south will start near that number. The Angels make sense on paper. Aitken was born in California, and a contender in Anaheim could sell him a short drive and a starting job. But Aitken is an Oakland native, and his whole life is here. He owns his place in Jack London, where he lives with his wife and three kids. He is the A's player rep and community liaison, he runs Aitken Little Leaguers, free baseball for East Oakland kids now going into its sixth year, and he shows up at city council and planning hearings without ever testifying, the way he brought Benji Dillon to the DEIR session. He was a major voice in the Baylight negotiations, and he was the veteran who reached out to Kevin Clark the day Clark got the call. On the parade bus after the World Series he said he was watching Vinnie Keane and Benji Dillon take in their last ride, and that he was taking it in too, "for a different reason.
